'''Wendy Alison Nelson''' {{postnominals|country=NZL|MNZM}} is a [[New Zealand]] marine scientist and world expert in [[phycology]]. She is New Zealand's leading authority on [[seaweed]]s.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://blog.tepapa.govt.nz/2016/07/20/nancy-adams-wendy-nelson-and-the-three-kings-seaweeds/|title=Nancy Adams, Wendy Nelson and the Three Kings' seaweeds|access-date=6 August 2017|date=19 July 2016}}</ref> Nelson is particularly interested in the [[biosystematics]] of seaweeds/[[macroalgae]] of New Zealand, with research on [[floristics]], evolution and [[phylogeny]], as well as [[ecology]], and life history studies of marine algae.  Recently she has worked on the systematics and biology of red algae including [[coralline algae]], distribution and diversity of seaweeds in harbours and soft sediment habitats, and seaweeds of the [[Ross Sea]] and [[Balleny Islands]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.niwa.co.nz/people/wendy-nelson|title=Dr Wendy Nelson|website=NIWA|language=en|access-date=11 October 2018}}</ref>

== Education ==
Nelson was born in [[Dunedin]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|last=Knight|first=Kim|url=https://www.pressreader.com/new-zealand/weekend-herald-canvas/20200328/282321092099631|title=Beyond Sushi|date=28 March 2020|department=Canvas|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|pages=10–14}}</ref> As a child she describes herself as obsessed with rock pools, beginning [[snorkeling]] at age 12, and was strongly influenced by Morton and Miller's 1968 book ''The New Zealand Seashore''.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last=Nicholls|first=Jenny|date=April 2020|title=Endless Forms Most Beautiful|journal=North & South|pages=87–88}}</ref> She completed a BSc at the [[University of Auckland]] in 1975, then a BSc Hons at [[Victoria University of Wellington]], before heading to Vancouver, Canada, to do her PhD at the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz/profile/wendy-nelson|title=Professor Wendy Nelson|access-date=6 August 2017|archive-date=6 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170806061041/https://unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz/profile/wendy-nelson|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{CiteQ|Q132874317}}</ref>

== Professional life ==

Nelson started working at [[Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa|New Zealand's National Museum]] in the 1970s, where she studied with her mentor [[Nancy Adams]].<ref name=":0" /> She was appointed Curator of Botany at the National Museum when Nancy Adams retired in 1987.<ref name=":0" /> From 1987 to 2002, she documented the national museum's seaweed collections, and added almost 8,000 new specimens.<ref name=":0" /> She moved to the [[National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research]] (NIWA) in 2002, where she is principal scientist and programme leader in marine biology, and is currently a Professor of Biological Sciences at the University of Auckland.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz/profile/wendy-nelson|title=Professor Wendy Nelson – The University of Auckland|website=unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz|access-date=6 August 2017|archive-date=6 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170806061041/https://unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz/profile/wendy-nelson|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.niwa.co.nz/people/wendy-nelson|title=Dr Wendy Nelson|website=NIWA|language=en|access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref>

Nelson is involved in a number of different projects cataloguing and describing marine algae from around New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz/profile/wendy-nelson|title=Professor Wendy Nelson – The University of Auckland|website=unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz|access-date=11 October 2018|archive-date=6 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170806061041/https://unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz/profile/wendy-nelson|url-status=dead}}</ref> She is also involved in the CARIM (Coastal acidification – rate, impacts and management)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.carim.nz/|title=Home|website=CARIM|language=en-NZ|access-date=11 October 2018}}</ref> research project funded by the [[Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment|Ministry of Business Innovation and Employment]]. The project is generating new knowledge on ocean acidification, to enhance protection and management of New Zealand coastal ecosystems.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.carim.nz/meet-our-team/|title=Team|website=CARIM|language=en-US|access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref> In 2019 she was principal author of a [[Department of Conservation (New Zealand)|Department of Conservation]] report on the conservation status of New Zealand macroalgae, which classified 609 of 938 species as data deficient and two as critically endangered.<ref name=":3" /> She has published over 185 peer-reviewed papers and four books, one as editor.<ref name=":4" />

Nelson was a member of the New Zealand Conservation Authority for eight years.<ref name=":2" /> She was re-appointed on 7 August 2020 for a further three-year term.<ref>{{Cite web|date=7 August 2020|title=Appointments to the New Zealand Conservation Authority|url=https://gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/2020-go3575|access-date=12 November 2020|website=New Zealand Gazette}}</ref> In 2015 she led the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]] report on the "National Taxonomic Collections of New Zealand."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Bootham|first=Laura|url= https://www.radionz.co.nz/news/national/292232/warning-of-grave-threat-to-species-collections |title=Warning of grave threat to species collections|date=15 December 2015|work=Radio New Zealand|access-date=11 October 2018|language=en-nz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=National Taxonomic Collections of New Zealand|date=December 2015|title=National Taxonomic Collections in New Zealand|url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/assets/Uploads/Report-National-Taxonomic-Collections-in-New-Zealand-2015.pdf|journal=Royal Society of New Zealand Report|via=Royal Society of New Zealand}}</ref> She was for two years the president of the International Phycological Society.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://intphycsociety.org/|title=International Phycological Society – Promoting phycology around the world|website=intphycsociety.org|language=en-US|access-date=11 October 2018}}</ref><ref name=":4" />

== Honours and awards ==
In 1996, Nelson was named winner of the Zonta Science Award.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zonta Science Award: Album of Winners 1990-2014 |url=https://zonta.org.nz/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/ALBUM-OF-WINNERS-1990-2014.pdf |access-date=9 May 2023}}</ref> The prize included an 'around the world airline ticket' to visit herbariums in Europe.<ref>{{cite news |title=Winner entangled by seaweed |publisher= The Dominion |date=31 May 1996}}</ref>

In the [[2008 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|2008 Queen's Birthday Honours]], Nelson was appointed a [[Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], for services to the marine environment.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.niwa.co.nz/publications/wa/vol16-no2-june-2008/news-queens-birthday-honour-for-dr-wendy-nelson-giant-squid-joins-its-colossal-mate-sobering|title=News: Queen's Birthday honour for Dr Wendy Nelson|date=1 June 2008|work=NIWA.co.nz|access-date=6 August 2017|publisher=National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research|language=en}}</ref>

In 2016, Nelson won the [[Royal Society Te Apārangi|Royal Society of New Zealand]]'s [[Hutton Medal]], which is awarded for outstanding work by a researcher in New Zealand in the Earth, plant and animal sciences.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://www.carim.nz/news/2016/26/11/carim-scientist-wendy-nelson-wins-prestigious-research-award|title=CARIM scientist Wendy Nelson wins prestigious research award|work=CARIM|access-date=6 August 2017|language=en-US}}</ref> The Royal Society commented: "She has significantly expanded knowledge of New Zealand seaweeds and the evolutionary relationships between seaweeds worldwide. She has also campaigned against seaweed pests and advanced understanding of the ecological importance of coral seaweeds and their [[Climate change vulnerability|vulnerability to climate change]]."<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/2016/11/23/celebrating-new-zealands-researchers/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161218043641/https://royalsociety.org.nz/2016/11/23/celebrating-new-zealands-researchers/|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 December 2016|title=Celebrating New Zealand's researchers « Media Releases « News « Royal Society of New Zealand|date=18 December 2016|access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref>

In 2017, Nelson was selected as one of the Royal Society Te Apārangi's "[[150 women in 150 words]]", celebrating the contributions of women to knowledge in New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wendy Nelson|url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/150th-anniversary/150-women-in-150-words/1968-2017/wendy-nelson/|access-date=2021-05-11|website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref>

In 2020 Nelson was awarded the [[Nancy Tyson Burbidge|Nancy Burbidge Medal]] by the [[Australasian Systematic Botany Society]], the society's highest honour.<ref name="Burbidge">{{cite web |title=Outstanding systematic scientist receives Australasian award |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/news/outstanding-systematic-scientist-receives-australasian-award/ |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref> Her Nancy T Burbidge lecture, titled "New perspectives on species recognition and the distribution of non-indigenous marine macroalgae in New Zealand", was given on 13 July 2021 (the 2020 conference was postonied due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].
<ref>{{cite web |title=Australasian Systematic Botany Society Annual Conference 2021 |url=https://asbs2021.bablglobal.com/talks/nancy-t-burbidge-lecture/ |website=Australasian Systematic Botany Society Annual Conference 2021 |access-date=13 July 2021 |archive-date=13 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210713061512/https://asbs2021.bablglobal.com/talks/nancy-t-burbidge-lecture/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Eponymy ==
Nelson has named and described 70 [[Taxon|taxa]], and has had a species and a genus named after her:<ref name=":4" />

* ''[[Skeletonella nelsoniae]]'' Millar and De Clerck, 2007
* ''[[Wendya]]'' D'Archino and Lin, 2016<ref>{{cite web |title=Wendya D'Archino & S.-M.Lin, 2016 |url=https://www.gbif.org/species/10439105 |website=www.gbif.org |access-date=23 August 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
